purpose: Vericiguat is used to lower the risk of hospitalization and death in adults who have chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction — meaning the heart is not pumping as well as it should. It is typically used in people who have recently had a worsening of their heart failure symptoms. It helps the heart work more efficiently and reduces strain on it.
how_it_works: Your heart relies on a chemical signal involving something called nitric oxide to help relax and widen blood vessels. In heart failure, this signal becomes weak. Vericiguat works by stimulating a protein called soluble guanylate cyclase, which boosts that signal even when nitric oxide levels are low. This helps relax blood vessels, lowers the workload on your heart, and improves blood flow throughout your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are low blood pressure (you may feel dizzy or lightheaded, especially when standing up quickly) and anemia (low red blood cell count, which can make you feel tired or weak). These are usually manageable but let your doctor or pharmacist know if they bother you.
warnings: Do not take vericiguat if you are pregnant — it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant must use reliable birth control while taking this medicine. Do not take it with nitrates (like nitroglycerin) or PDE5 inhibitors (like sildenafil/Viagra) because combining these can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Always tell your healthcare team about all medications you take.
typical_dosing: You usually start with a low dose of 2.5 mg taken by mouth once a day with food. Your doctor will gradually increase the dose every two weeks as tolerated, aiming for a target dose of 10 mg once daily. Always take it with a meal to help your body absorb it properly, and take it at the same time each day.
